key_insight: Semantic dispersion among sibling actions predicts downstream redundancy, enabling LLM tree-search budgets to be allocated before expansion rather than fixed uniformly.
engineering_relevance: Training-free adaptive allocation can reduce inference cost and latency while maintaining comparable reasoning accuracy.
method: Use candidate values to identify promising branches and sibling dispersion to estimate uncertainty without additional model calls.
Apply uncertainty-aware pruning and budgeting to control which candidates expand and how much computation they receive.
Motivate allocation with an information-theoretic sufficient budget that shrinks as sibling dispersion increases.
evidence_signal: Across mathematical reasoning, logical reasoning, and planning benchmarks, UAA reports up to 90% lower token usage and up to 9× speedup at comparable accuracy across four tree-search algorithms and open- and closed-source LLMs.
watch_item: Reported savings are best-case; deployment should validate whether sibling dispersion reliably predicts downstream redundancy for the target model and task.
paper_title: Uncertainty-Aware Budget Allocation for Efficient LLM Tree Search
